transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-09-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~62m | Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Jamie Chen (Redwood SE), Rita Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Rao (Lynxbridge Head of ML), Marcus Li (Eng Manager), Elena Torres (FinOps)

Summary: quick sync to triage August billing spike, talk short-term Dedicated pilot, and scope a technical deep dive for KV/prefix cache perf. Some sections auto-generated by Fireflies.

[00:00] Alex: ok hey everyone thanks for carving time, quick roll call, if you could say hi and role really quick?
[00:10] Priya: hi this is Priya Rao, Head of ML at Lynxbridge, running the recommender and conversational surfaces, thanks for setting this up.
[00:18] Marcus: Marcus Li, engineering manager for inference platform.
[00:22] Elena: Elena Torres, FinOps - will ask the hard questions.
[00:26] Alex: great, Alex here AE, and Jamie is our SE, Rita on CSM. Jamie you want to jump into the usage/cost notes?
[00:33] Jamie: yeah sure, so we looked at the August window the main datapoint was a 3.4x increase in token volume on the 8/12-8/19 window, it correlates with the new onboarding flow you rolled out, there was also a bump in mean sequence length — a lot of 4k+ sequences which pushed you into longer compute paths and fewer effective batches.
[01:00] Priya: correct, our support chat integration started sending full conversation history on every request — we realized after the fact the client didn't truncate the context — so that created the long tails.
[01:12] Elena: and we saw the invoice, yeah that was painful, need to figure causal attribution and a short term cap.
[01:19] Alex: understandable. two tracks: immediate guardrails + billing controls (rate limits, request size caps, token quotas) and medium term Dedicated pilot where you can lock capacity/price.
[01:33] Marcus: curious on the Dedicated sizing. we have bursts — traffic goes from 50 RPS to 350 for a ten minute window. does Dedicated handle that gracefully?
[01:42] Jamie: depends on autoscale policy; for a pilot we recommend a fixed 1-shard Dedicated with controlled autoscale off so you measure steady-state economics, then enable burst buffer / burst capacity to absorb spikes. it's a common pattern we use for pilots to get repeatable unit cost numbers.
[02:02] Priya: can you clarify shard = gpu pool size? we still get mixed terms.
[02:06] Jamie: yes shard ~ single Dedicated GPU pool instance - for your model family we'd likely recommend 4 A100-equivalent vram, we got initial perf numbers from you from June.
[02:18] Elena: cost question: if we reserve one shard for 2 weeks what is the expected burn vs hosted? we need a forecast.
[02:25] Alex: I'll send a tiered pricing sheet — quick estimate: reserved shard for two weeks roughly equals 0.8x the peak hosted cost for heavy convo workloads because you get batching + KV cache gains but you lose some burst flexibility; exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[02:40] Priya: about the KV/prefix cache — our usage pattern is a lot of repeated prefixes across users but with small per-user slots. The cache miss rate looked high in your dashboard. what did you see?
[02:54] Jamie: our telemetry shows eviction rates high for messages > 4096 tokens because the current config uses per-shard fixed cache windows; for large context flows KV segments push out older entries. we can tune max entries and eviction policy and there's also a new compacting strategy in the runtime that helps with long-context workloads.
[03:15] Marcus: is that something you can change without code changes on our side? we prefer config knobs not SDK changes.
[03:20] Jamie: yes, most are server-side runtime knobs, we can flip cache window, set prefix aggregation and save you from rewriting clients. but some efficiency wins do come from truncating upstream requests.
[03:32] Elena: security/regulatory quick round — we need SOC2 type II docs, KMS/HSM integration for keys, and data residency confirmation. what do you provide?
[03:45] Rita: we have SOC2 docs and encryption at rest + in transit details, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and on-prem options, and for Hosted we offer strict key management integrations. I'll drop the SOC2 pack and an architecture note.
[04:00] Priya: do you support per-tenant encryption keys? that was a request from compliance.
[04:04] Rita: yes via our KMS integration in Private, and in Dedicated we can arrange customer keys on request — there's a short legal addendum for bring-your-own-key.
[04:12] Marcus: timeline and stakeholders — we need to budget for Q4 pilot and decide procurement path. Procurement will want a predictable cap.
[04:20] Elena: yes, procurement likely needs a 3 month estimate and a PO path.
[04:24] Alex: recommendation: 2-week Dedicated pilot starting mid-October, we provide a fixed shard and controlled autoscale, bench numbers, then a 30-day economics readout. We can produce a PO-ready quote.
[04:37] Priya: 2-week pilot seems ok. we want to measure latency percentiles under production load and token cost per effective response.
[04:45] Jamie: for latency we will run both synthetic traffic and replay your 7-day history — that's where we ask you for the traffic histogram and top prompt list.
[04:55] Priya: noted. we'll sanitize and send night-of.
[05:00] Elena: any immediate guardrails we can flip while pilot is in flight to prevent another billing surprise?
[05:06] Jamie: yes rate limiting per-route, a soft token cap with alerts, and request size enforcement. we can set a temporary soft quota for the support channel to 2k tokens per request.
[05:18] Marcus: will that break the user experience? some flows need 3k tokens occasionally.
[05:23] Priya: we can degrade gracefully: short-term truncation, then button to load more.
[05:28] Alex: ok, action: we'll configure a 2k soft cap for a week and monitor.
[05:33] [small cross talk about who owns the SDK change]
[05:40] Jamie: on deployment strategy, if you plan to move to Private later we can capture the same config as a helm chart and keep rollout policies identical so your SREs have a single operational playbook.
[05:54] Priya: timeline question — if pilot runs mid-Oct and looks good, when can Dedicated become full-reserved?
[05:59] Alex: after pilot we recommend a staged reservation: 1 shard for 30 days, then evaluate at 30-day mark; legal lead time often 2-4 weeks for enterprise PO.
[06:15] Elena: let's talk about dashboarding — we need token-level cost by route and latency percentiles split by model variant. is that available?
[06:22] Rita: Redwood Console shows per-route token spend, model breakdown, and latency p95/p99; we can add a custom dashboard and push CSV exports to S3.
[06:33] Marcus: we noticed some model fallbacks in the logs — requests get routed to a smaller quantized variant during capacity events, can you explain the fallback policy?
[06:44] Jamie: yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible quantized variants — in the dashboard you can turn off automatic fallback or restrict to certain models; fallback reduces quality slightly but keeps latency.
[06:54] Priya: important — we need a canary policy so only a small percentage hits the fallback model.
[07:00] Jamie: we can set canary to 5% with automatic rollback on quality regressions.
[07:08] Alex: ok, recording to action items and next steps. any blockers on the pilot?
[07:13] Priya: internal: procurement sign-off and we need the initial quote. technical: none, but we want KV-cache perf test first.
[07:20] Elena: quote must include an explicit burst policy and expected overage behavior.
[07:24] Alex: will include burst policy and overage terms.
[07:28] Marcus: one technical ask — can Redwood run the pilot with a slightly older model version to match our on-device quantization? we want apples-to-apples.
[07:36] Jamie: yes we can pin model version, we support custom model artifacts in Dedicated, but we need to vet the artifact for runtime compatibility.
[07:45] Priya: ok good.
[07:48] [moderate pause, attendees typing]
[08:05] Alex: quick recap: 1) two-week Dedicated pilot mid-Oct, 1 shard, autoscale off; 2) Alex sends pricing and PO-ready quote; 3) Jamie runs KV-cache perf tests with your prompt set; 4) Rita shares SOC2/KMS docs; 5) Priya shares traffic histograms and prompts.
[08:30] Priya: timeline acceptance, we'll aim to return final sign-off by 2027-10-02.
[08:35] Alex: perfect, we'll target pilot start 2027-10-16 pending procurement.
[08:40] Elena: who owns the ticketing after the pilot? CSM or AE?
[08:44] Rita: CSM will own the pilot coordination and success metrics, AE supports commercials.
[08:49] Marcus: one last quick perf question — what's realistic p99 under 4k token loads on Dedicated for our model? any ballpark numbers?
[08:56] Jamie: ballpark p99 is around 420-520ms depending on batching; we'll verify during the KV test.
[09:05] Priya: great. thanks everyone.
[09:09] Alex: thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts, and schedule the tech deep dive next week.
[09:15] Meeting ended.
